sections.title: Cold Weather Starting With or Without Pre-Heat

items.text: Brief passengers on use of belts/harnesses and requirements for wearing them.

items.response: Off (take key out and hang it up)
Prime engine two to four strokes (up to seven without pre-heat) while propeller is turned by hand

items.text: With ignition switch off and throttle closed, prime the engine two to four strokes (up to seven without pre-heat) as the propeller is being turned by hand. Use heavy primer strokes for best atomization of fuel.
If doing this by yourself, tie the plane down securely and set parking brake, in case engine starts.
Treat propeller as if the ignition is on and engine could start. Leave primer charged and ready for a stroke.

items.response: Pump to full open twice then return to 1/4 inch open position
Continue to prime until engine is running smoothly. Alternately pump throttle rapidly over first 1/4 of travel

items.text: This might take a little time since the engine is cold. If pressure doesn't come up in about 30 seconds, shut the engine down.

items.response: Full on after engine started. Leave on until running smoothly

items.text: If engine does not start during the first few attempts, or if engine firing diminishes in strength, it is probable that the spark plugs have frosted over. Pre-heat must be used before another start is attempted.

Pumping the throttle may cause raw fuel to accumulate in the intake air duct, creating a fire hazard in the event of a back-fire. If this occurs, maintain a cranking action to suck flames into the engine. An outside attendant with a fire extinguisher is advised for cold starts without pre-heat.
3. Perform steps 3 and 4 on normal start checklist
Set attitude indicator to level flight position; Set altimeter to runway altitude or locally reported altimeter setting; Set heading indicator to magnetic compass.
RPM drop should not exceed 125 RPM on either magneto. RPM difference between magnetos should not exceed 50 RPM.
